findings.issue: MARKET AGGREGATION (H1b): breadth-based M beat v1's expanding z-score of mean Z on dev walk-forward, then lost to it on 2026 five-session changes (-0.035, CI -0.077 to +0.001).
findings.diagnosis:
ROOT CAUSE: the loss comes from the frozen dev percentile scale, not from using breadth as the aggregate. The walk-forward selected logit breadth BL = logit(mean_i P_i(not calm)), and the +0.037 gain was measured on BL. v2 then froze something different, M = Phi^-1(F_dev(BL)). That map was never scored on changes.

Evidence (5-session-change Spearman with VXN; paired stationary bootstrap, mean block 20, 2000 resamples; s.e. = bootstrap s.d.):
(1) Dev walk-forward out-of-sample, cached S1 fold fits, each fold using its own training m_map. This comparison was declared in candidates.md before scoring. M_foldmap 0.618 vs BL 0.661: diff -0.043 (s.e. 0.015, CI -0.072 to -0.012). Pearson -0.107 (s.e. 0.035). All three folds are negative (-0.013, -0.016, -0.074). z is -2.6, -2.8 and -3.1 at blocks 10, 20 and 40. On dev, what v2 froze never beat legacy: M_foldmap minus Mleg = -0.005 (s.e. 0.015). The +0.037 was BL minus Mleg (reproduced: s.e. 0.017, z 2.26).
(2) 2026, frozen spec, diagnosis only. Each step of the chain: raw B 0.617 → logit BL 0.603 (logit effect -0.014, s.e. 0.010, not significant) → M 0.548 (map effect -0.055, s.e. 0.020, CI -0.091 to -0.015; Pearson -0.122, s.e. 0.028). v1-published legacy is 0.583. BL minus v1 = +0.020 (s.e. 0.022): the same sign as dev, about half the size. Leaving out any one month shifts H1b by at most 0.012, so no single episode drives it.

MECHANISM: dev breadth is right-skewed (57% of dev days have B < 0.3; the tail runs to 0.97). The normalising map Phi^-1∘F_dev is therefore concave across the occupied range. Frozen map dM/dB is 14.1 for B < 0.2, 7.7 for 0.2–0.3, 5.0 for 0.3–0.4, and 2.5–3.1 for 0.4–0.8. VXN responds to breadth changes the other way, more strongly at higher levels. The slope of dVXN on dB rises from about 7–10 (B < 0.3) to 13–17 (0.3–0.6) to 23–25 (0.6–0.8) on dev, and the 2026 values match. So the map amplifies noise in calm periods and compresses the mid/high-stress changes VXN reacts to. 2026 spent 49% of its days at B 0.4–0.7, against 20% on dev. Median map gain on 2026 days was 4.5, against 7.5 on dev days, so the cost grew.

Relative gain per unit dB, lowest to highest bin, 2026:
- M: 2.07 → 0.57–0.61
- v1 legacy: 1.58 → 0.78–0.84
- BL: 1.33 → 0.85–0.94
- B: flat
- VXN: 0.34 → 1.94

The more concave a reading is in B, the worse its 2026 change correlation (M 0.548 < legacy 0.583 < BL 0.603 < B 0.617). v1 beat M only because its own nonlinearity (per-stock maps, then averaged) is milder.

OTHER MECHANISMS RULED OUT, with evidence:
- Expanding z-score adapting to 2026: corr(dMleg, dZbar/sd_t) = 0.99992 and yardstick drift is 0.015% of dMleg variance. sd_t moved only from 0.598 to 0.601 during 2026. C3 (fixed yardstick) ≈ expanding legacy: dev +0.008 (s.e. 0.006).
- Saturation: B peaked at 0.889 in 2026, against 0.968 on dev. Stock-days with P(not calm) > 0.99 were 2.03% in 2026 vs 1.99% on dev. No 2026 day fell outside the m_map knot range.
- Severity gradient: in 2026, dB explains even more of d(mean severity) (R² 0.93, vs 0.86 on dev). 2026 had less panic per unit breadth (P(panic)/B 0.117 vs 0.138). Mean severity loses on dev (C2: -0.047, s.e. 0.016).
- IPO composition: no stock entered the eligible set in 2026 (134 eligible from 2025Q3; 133 on the last two days because of the masked SNDK bar).

IMPLICATION: 'no change' below means keep breadth on the logit scale, the aggregate dev selected. It does not mean keep v2's percentile scale for the index whose changes are tracked. No new candidate is needed: v3 should ship the selected object faithfully as M_v3 = (BL - mu_dev)/sd_dev, a fixed linear yardstick. F_M = 100·F_dev(BL) can stay as a display percentile. Because the map preserves rank, levels, bands and alert days are unchanged: BL ≥ 1.2376 ⇔ M ≥ 2, which is the same 4 days in 2026. Post hoc 2026 for that fix: H1 0.603 vs 0.548. H1b analogue vs v1 +0.020 (CI -0.024 to +0.062): no longer worse, but still 'not claimed'.

findings.issue: TAIL FORECAST CALIBRATION (H2): q_next had a dev walk-forward slope of 0.98 but 0.80 in 2026, with the top bins over-predicting.
findings.diagnosis:
The 2026 result is not a new failure. The pooled dev slope of 0.98 averaged two opposite errors that cancelled on dev but not in 2026. Inputs reproduced exactly: dev OOS slope 0.9838 (s.e. 0.188), Brier 0.037836 on 48,851 stock-days; 2026 slope 0.8014 (s.e. 0.118), Brier 0.034887 on 30,148 stock-days.

(1) The dev folds disagree with each other. Logistic slopes with day-clustered s.e. are 1.31 (0.63) for 2024H2, 1.35 (0.30) for 2025H1 and 0.65 (0.16) for 2025H2. Cochran Q = 4.9 on 2 df, p = 0.09; the precision-weighted slope is 0.83 (0.14). The latest fold, whose model is closest to the frozen one, already over-predicted: mean q 3.36% against 2.80% observed, intercept -1.32. 2026 is 1.68 s.e. below a slope of 1 (p = 0.09), 0.82 s.e. below the pooled dev 0.98, and 0.76 s.e. above fold C.

(2) Splitting the slope shows two separate errors. I regressed the event on the day's mean logit q (between-day) and on each stock's distance from that mean (within-day), with day-clustered s.e.
- Within-day slope: 0.50 (0.07) on dev OOS (0.31, 0.74, 0.43 by fold) and 0.73 (0.12) in 2026. It is below 1 in every period (dev z = -7.1, 2026 z = -2.2), so the spread of forecasts across stocks on a given day is consistently too wide.
- Between-day slope: 1.43 (0.32) on dev (2.53, 1.84, 0.95 by fold) and 0.95 (0.36) in 2026. It depends on whether a few market-wide episodes continued (Aug 2024, Apr 2025) or rebounded.
On dev the two cancelled to 0.98; in 2026 the between-day part was neutral, so the within-day error showed through as 0.80.

(3) Why the within-day spread is too wide. Take stocks hit (x >= 3) at t-1 while fewer than 10% of stocks were hit, i.e. stock-specific shocks such as earnings. Observed/forecast was 0.67 on dev (t = -2.1, 228 days) and 0.74 in 2026 (t = -1.5, 138 days). Stocks whose forecast stood far above the day's mean (q >= 0.05, logit gap >= 1) were 0.59 on dev (t = -3.7). One transition matrix is shared by all stocks, and its stress persistence is learned mostly from market-wide crashes. It therefore treats a one-day stock-specific shock as if it would persist like a crash.

(4) The 2026 top-bin shortfall comes from a few market rebound days. Forecasts q >= 0.075 covered 1,373 stock-days on 169 days, with 97 events against 128.1 expected. Six days just after market-wide shock days account for 27.2 of the 31.1 shortfall:
- 2026-11-06: 98 high-forecast stocks, 9.1 expected, 0 observed.
- 2026-06-08: 6.0 expected, 0 observed.
- 2026-11-23: 3.5 expected, 0 observed.
- 2026-07-06: 3.3 expected, 0 observed.
- 2026-03-04: 2.7 expected, 0 observed.
- 2026-02-06: 3.5 expected, 1 observed.
A shock day here means at least 20% of stocks had x >= 3. After 5 of the 7 shock days in 2026, the next session's event share was 0.8% or less. On dev the day after a shock was under-predicted instead (q 6.0% against 15.9%). Outcomes on the same day move together: the day-level design effect is 15 to 50 (19.9 in 2026), so the effective sample is roughly the number of days, not stock-days.

(5) 2026-11-05 was a crash day: 90 of 134 stocks hit, 7.5 expected. The hits were concentrated among high-forecast stocks (17 of 23), so this day pulls the slope up; dropping it gives 0.741. The over-prediction belongs to the next day, 11-06.

(6) Mechanisms that were ruled out:
- Slow-adapting sigma: the 21-day over 126-day robust scale ratio was 1.09, 1.15, 1.01 and 1.00 by 2026 quarter, inside dev's 0.85 to 1.17 range. The overall level was right (mean q 3.80% against 3.65% observed), and the low bins were only slightly under-predicted (t about 0.6).
- Over-persistent transition matrix: 3 to 5 days after a shock, 2026 forecasts were above outcomes (0.055 vs 0.020; 0.045 vs 0.027), but dev shows the reverse (0.044 vs 0.075; 0.039 vs 0.076).
- Half-normal tail shape in stressed states: in high-panic forecast groups, 2026 over-predicts every threshold from 2 to 6 by a similar proportion, while dev under-predicts thresholds 1 to 4. The error is in how much stress follows, not in the shape of the tail at 3. Only the far tail x >= 6 is over-predicted in both periods (1.40% vs 0.65% on dev, 1.46% vs 0.61% in 2026), which barely moves the x >= 3 event.

One instability worth noting: the stressed state's tail probability moved from 0.023 to 0.034 to 0.056 across folds as the stressed scale rose from 1.36 to 1.66.

findings.issue: VOLATILITY INCREMENT (H4): the frozen-coefficient HAR forecast of 5-day log basket volatility had negative 2026 OOS R^2 (-0.041), and M's increment was insignificant (DM-HLN t 0.86).
findings.diagnosis:
Two separate things went wrong. Neither is caused by M being on a percentile scale.

(1) The negative R^2 comes from a level shift combined with an oracle benchmark. 2026 mean log 5-day vol was -3.750, against -4.063 on dev: +0.313 (HAC s.e. 0.064), roughly 37% vs 27% annualised. The frozen HAR's slopes sum to 0.57, so it reverts toward its dev-implied level of -4.15. Its 2026 mean forecast was -3.909, a bias of +0.158 (HAC s.e. 0.046) that accounts for 17% of the MSE. The published OOS R^2 uses the 2026 sample mean as its benchmark, so the benchmark already knows 2026's level. Against the feasible dev-mean benchmark (Campbell-Thompson), HAR scores +0.383 and HAR+M +0.414.

(2) The slopes are not the problem. The Mincer-Zarnowitz slope on 2026 is 0.98 (s.e. 0.28). A HAC Wald test for a change in the slopes between dev and 2026 gives 1.37 on 3 df (HAR) and 1.57 on 4 df (HAR+M). Moving only the intercept to the 2026 mean removes 97% of the frozen model's extra MSE over a full 2026 refit (MSE 0.1483 frozen, 0.1233 with the oracle intercept, 0.1226 with a full refit).

(3) M's increment did not weaken; the test lacks power. The 2026 MSE gain of HAR+M over HAR (0.0074) is the same as the dev in-sample gain (0.0078). It comes entirely from the variance term (bias term 3e-5). On demeaned errors the DM-HLN t is 0.85. In 2026, M stays inside its dev range, with no upper-tail extrapolation and no floor hits. Its partial correlation with the HAR residual is 0.23 on dev and 0.25 in 2026. Logit breadth (0.27/0.25) and mean logit severity (0.26/0.26) behave the same way. Scaling the effect sizes to n=220 gives an expected t of 1.29 (dev walk-forward B0 effect) or 1.01 (recursive design). The power of the pre-registered one-sided 5% test was therefore about 36% or 26%. Reaching 80% power at the recursive-design effect would take about 1,340 sessions (about 5 years).

(4) The level problem is not specific to 2026. The dev walk-forward baseline has it too. Training-window means were -4.25, -4.16 and -4.05, against test-half means of -3.96, -3.74 and -4.11. The per-fold fixed HAR+M has stitched OOS bias +0.214 (HAC s.e. 0.043) and oracle R^2 -0.19. Its coefficients are unstable on short windows: fold A, with one year (242 obs), has a monthly-lag coefficient of -0.65 and a slope sum of -0.55.

(5) Mechanism for M's information. In a level-free HAR (slopes constrained to sum to 1), M's coefficient is about 0 in every fold (t 0.05, -0.04, -0.24) and its dev OOS increment is -0.0001. M correlates 0.27-0.42 with RV5-RV22. Much of what M adds is information about how persistent the current vol level is, which a model anchored to a fixed mean otherwise lacks.

findings.overfitting_risks:
What the adoption covers: only the H4 forecasting design. The HAR and HAR+M coefficients are re-estimated daily on an expanding window using only observed targets (s <= t-5), from 2023-07-07. The fear signal, M, its maps and every frozen parameter stay unchanged. The rule was fixed in candidates.md before scoring: HLN t > 1, at least 2 of 3 folds positive, gain mechanism as predicted, largest gain among qualifiers. C1 meets it under every kernel and resampling check. Under the adopted design H4 is still not supported, either on dev OOS (t 1.31) or in 2026 post hoc (t 0.78), so the change does not tilt the result toward passing.

Risks and caveats:
(a) The candidates were motivated partly by the 2026 level-shift diagnosis. The same shift is visible in the dev walk-forward baseline (bias +0.214, s.e. 0.043), so the mechanism is not 2026-specific.
(b) C1's dev gain is concentrated in fold A, the one-year training window. Without fold A it is +0.015 (t 1.25). With the 2.5+ year windows a prospective test will use, the expected gain is small: 2026 post hoc it is +0.0066.
(c) C2 and C3 also nominally cleared one s.e. (t 1.01 and 1.11). Three of three candidates passing the primary bar at t of about 1 is roughly what noise in a handful of vol episodes can produce. C2 collapses when fold A is dropped (t -0.30) or with long kernels. C3 fails its mechanism check, and its 2026 sign reverses (post hoc). Neither should be revisited.
(d) The R^2 change is a reporting correction, not a forecast improvement. R^2 against the training mean (+0.38) should be shown next to the published oracle-benchmark R^2 (-0.04), not instead of it. H4's pre-registered pass criterion was the DM test, and this correction leaves that test untouched.
(e) An expanding window still adapts slowly: the 2026 bias under C1 is +0.144. Rolling windows and intercept correction would need a window length, which is a free tuning choice; they were deliberately not tried, to avoid forking.
(f) H4 cannot be decided on one year of data. Power is about 26-36% at n=220, and about 5 years are needed for 80% power. A future H4 should be pre-registered with C1 and a multi-year horizon, or dropped as a headline claim.
(g) No 2026 number fed any choice. All 2026 figures for the candidates are post-hoc diagnostics. The repo is untouched (git status clean).

findings.issue: Overfitting-control protocol for a v3 revision after the 2026 holdout has been spent. Deliverables: a tested Hansen (2005) SPA implementation (SPA_c, SPA_l, SPA_u, stationary bootstrap, NW / SB-kernel / bootstrap variance), its application to the committed dev walk-forward log scores, and a v3 protocol with a prospective holdout and a power analysis.
findings.diagnosis:
Mechanism behind 2026 not replicating dev wins (H1b: dev breadth gain +0.037, CI 0.001-0.066, became -0.035 in 2026; H2 passed at the boundary): selection was pairwise with no family-wise control, and the evidence rests on a handful of crash days, so dev-period inference is far more liberal than its nominal level. Evidence, all from dev-only resampling, none from 2026:

(1) In the 378 stitched dev test days, the 5 largest days carry 57-77% of the variance of the S2/S3/S5-minus-S1 daily log-score differentials (2025-01-27 DeepSeek; 2025-04-03/04/07 tariffs). Kurtosis is 15-80.

(2) At that covariance (stationary bootstrap of the observed demeaned differentials, block 10, R=1000), the rule "adopt if a candidate beats the incumbent by >= 1 NW(10) s.e." falsely adopts 47.5% of the time under the least-favourable null and 33.9% under the mixed null. Parametric Monte Carlo (T=380, t5, AR(0.3), cross-correlation 0.6) gives 36/47/54% for K=4/8/12.

(3) Even Hansen's SPA_c is oversized here: 12.9% at nominal 5% with fixed studentisation, 9-12% with the bootstrap-t. In the parametric Monte Carlo it is 6.9/8.5/9.1% for K=4/8/12. Diagnosis runs: iid data with block 1 give 5.3% (the code is right); block 10 gives 7.5% (5.7% with the true variance), so the oversize comes from noise in the variance estimate. The bootstrap-t fixes the parametric case (3.8-6.8%) but not the crash-day case: a sample that misses a rare loss day cannot learn it exists.

(4) Calibrating the level in the bootstrap world (two-world prepivoting, spa_calibrated, recomputed on each of 200 synthetic samples) gives 5.0% (least-favourable) and 3.5% (mixed) at nominal 5%, with 67% power for an S2-like gain of +0.003 nats/obs. A one-world version gave 7.0% / 12.0%. On the real S2-S5 family the implied raw level is 0.009.

Part (b) answers:
- No candidate in S2-S5 beats S1. All mean differentials are negative (nats/obs: -0.00062, -0.00106, -0.00989, -0.00050; t = -0.85, -1.10, -3.26, -0.43), so T_SPA = 0 and p_c = p_l = p_u = 1.00 for blocks 5/10/20/40, every variance estimator, and fixed, bootstrap-t and calibrated versions alike. The 90% model confidence set is {S1, S2, S3, S5} with MCS p-values 1.00 / 0.78 / 0.45 / 0.78; S4 is eliminated (p = 0.003). The most parsimonious member is S1, the same choice as the committed 1-SE rule.
- S1 never beats S0 (p = 1). S0 leads S1 by +0.00547 nats/obs (t = 1.56). Raw p is 0.075 with fixed studentisation and 0.030 with the bootstrap-t; calibrated p is 0.047 (fixed) and 0.020 (bootstrap-t). That edge is look-ahead:
  - Per fold it is t = 0.57 / 1.79 / 0.53.
  - It is 85% carried by the 2024-08 yen-carry unwind and the 2025-04 tariff crash, which S1's fold-A and fold-B training windows had not yet seen. Dropping the 5 dominant episodes leaves +0.00084 (t = 0.45).
  - Post-hoc on 2026, where both are out of sample, it is -0.0002 (NW s.e. 0.0006, t = -0.33).

candidates.spec: Adopt any candidate that beats the incumbent by >= 1 NW(10) s.e. on the dev walk-forward (evaluate.FOLDS, per-fold parameters). Parsimony among candidates within 1 s.e. of the best. 2026 is spent and nothing prospective is pre-registered.
candidates.mechanism: Parsimony bias of the one-SE rule. Against it: each pairwise t > 1 test has about 16% size, so with K candidates the chance that at least one passes by luck grows with K. Heavy-tailed crash-day differentials make this worse.
candidates.dev_oos_result: Operating characteristics at the empirical dev covariance (stationary bootstrap, block 10, of the 378-day S2-S5-minus-S1 differentials; R=1000; MC s.e. about 1.6%). False adoption: 47.5% under the least-favourable null, 33.9% under the mixed null, 9.9-11.9% when every candidate is truly worse by its observed amount. Power: 95% at +0.002 and 99.6% at +0.003 nats/obs (S2-like). Parametric Monte Carlo (T=380): false adoption 36/47/54% for K=4/8/12.
candidates.post_hoc_2026: POST-HOC, spent holdout: the breadth gain this kind of selection found on dev (+0.037, CI 0.001-0.066) reversed in 2026 (-0.035, CI -0.077 to +0.001). That fits a winner's curse but is not evidence for selection.

candidates.name: P1: dev-only selection with one-SE plus a calibrated SPA_c family gate, Holm across issues, labelled 2026 post-hoc reporting, and a prospective holdout (RECOMMENDED)
candidates.spec:
Selection rules:
(i) At most 4 mechanism-motivated candidates per issue, declared in candidates.md and hashed into a ledger before scoring. Families are closed at declaration.
(ii) Dev walk-forward with per-fold parameters. Adopt only if all of: (a) the candidate beats the incumbent by >= 1 dependence-robust s.e. (NW(10) on daily losses; paired stationary-bootstrap s.e., block 20, on correlations); (b) spa.spa_calibrated(d, block=10, B=999, R=999)['p_c_calibrated'] for the whole family is below its Holm threshold (family-wise 0.10 across the round's issues, each threshold capped at 0.05); for correlation families use spa_functional_calibrated(block=20); (c) per-fold signs and leave-one-episode-out results are reported and fit the stated mechanism; (d) if several candidates pass, take the most parsimonious inside the 90% MCS.
(iii) 2026 numbers for every declared candidate, computed only after the dev decision, labelled post-hoc, in a separate table.

Freeze and prospective tests:
(iv) Re-estimate the selected spec on 2023-01-03..2026-11-23 by the same code path (estimation, not selection). Commit config/frozen_v3.json and the pre-registration before downloading any bar after 2026-11-23. Keep v2-frozen running as the comparator.
(v) One prospective read at N = 300 sessions after 2026-11-23 (about 2028-02-03); N = 400 (about 2028-06-28) if the team can wait. No interim looks. H1': Spearman of 5-session changes of M and VXN, lower bound > 0.30. H1b' (v3 vs v2 vs v1): minimum detectable effect is about 0.05. H2' is read with its published operating characteristics (P(pass | slope 0.8) = 0.50 at s.e. 0.102).
candidates.mechanism: SPA controls the family-wise false-adoption rate under data snooping. Consistent recentring stops hopeless candidates (e.g. K=2) from making the test conservative. Calibrating the level in the bootstrap world of the real dev sample corrects the 2-2.6x oversize caused by crash-day-dominated differentials. Holm handles the several issue families that agents fan out over. The prospective holdout is the only data v3 has not seen.
candidates.dev_oos_result: Same dev-covariance simulation as P0. False adoption under the least-favourable null: 4.0-4.5% for one-SE plus SPA_c at the calibrated raw level 0.0099 (R=1000), and 5.0% with spa_calibrated rerun on each sample (R=200, MC s.e. 1.5%). Under the mixed null: 0.7-1.0% and 3.5%. P0 is 47.5% and 33.9%. Power: 57-59% at +0.002 and 67-89% at +0.003 nats/obs for an S2-like differential (s.e. 0.00073), so 80% power needs about 0.003-0.004 nats/obs. Applied to the committed dev evidence it adopts nothing: S2-S5 vs S1 calibrated p = 1.00; MCS keeps S1. Correlation-family check: raw functional SPA 9.7% at 5% (R=300), calibrated 5.3% (R=150). Power analysis for the H1-type test (lower 95% bound > 0.30 when rho is about 0.55): analytic Fisher z with variance-inflation factor 2.15 (2026) / 2.81 (dev) needs 196-254 sessions for 80% power and 259-337 for 90%. Simulated power at 300 sessions: 0.88 (Gaussian, rho 0.552), 0.81 (2026 resampled, rho 0.527), 0.77 (dev attenuated, rho 0.533), 0.97 (dev raw, rho 0.627). At 400 sessions: 0.94 / 0.91 / 0.89 / 0.99. CI coverage at 300-400 sessions is 0.89-0.95, and 0.78-0.88 below 150, so no interim reads.
candidates.post_hoc_2026: POST-HOC, spent holdout, not used: S0 minus frozen S1 log score on 2026 is -0.0002 nats/obs (NW s.e. 0.0006, t = -0.33; S1-beats-S0 p = 0.36). This agrees with P1 adopting no stock-layer change and with S0's dev edge being look-ahead.

candidates.name: P2: P1 plus a reusable prospective holdout (Thresholdout, Dwork et al. 2015)
candidates.spec: Thresholdout on the prospective sample: threshold T, Laplace noise sigma, budget B. Answer the training (dev+2026) value unless |holdout - training| > T + Lap(4 sigma); otherwise answer holdout + Lap(sigma) and spend one unit of budget. Concrete parameters for the H1-type statistic at N=300: holdout s.e. of rho 0.07-0.08 and training s.e. about 0.05, so the gap s.d. is about 0.094, giving T = 0.19, sigma = T/4 = 0.047 (the paper's 0.04/0.01 ratio), B = 2-3. For log scores T is about 0.002-0.004 nats/obs.
candidates.mechanism: Lets the prospective sample be queried adaptively with bounded overfitting. It fails here: every effect the project must resolve (0.03-0.04 in rho; 0.0005-0.003 nats/obs) is below T, so it would almost always return the training value. When it does consult the holdout, Laplace noise (s.d. 0.067) widens the s.e. from 0.08 to 0.104, worth about 40% of the sample. Its iid guarantee does not hold for about 15 effective 20-session blocks. A one-shot pre-registered read needs no reuse.
candidates.dev_oos_result: Not simulated: rejected analytically from the noise/threshold arithmetic above, using simulation-based s.e. of rho at N=300 (sd of rho-hat 0.071-0.082). It adds no discrimination at the effect sizes of interest and costs about 40% of the effective sample.

findings.adopt_candidate: P1: dev-only selection with one-SE plus a calibrated SPA_c family gate, Holm across issues, labelled 2026 post-hoc reporting, and a prospective holdout (RECOMMENDED)
findings.overfitting_risks:
- **Approximate level.** The gate's actual level is only approximately 5%. The calibration world is the dev sample itself, and with 2-3 decisive crash episodes the level can be off by several points: 5.0% / 3.5% for the two-world prepivoting, 7.0% / 12.0% for a one-world version. Keep the threshold strict and do not over-read raw p-values.
- **Low power.** The calibrated gate needs about 0.003-0.004 nats/obs (stock layer) or about +0.08 in rho (market layer, 41% power raw) for 80% power. Most plausible v3 fixes will correctly end as "no change", and a failure to adopt is weak evidence of no effect.
- **Meta-level snooping.** This protocol was written after seeing 2026's failures, and the parameters below were set by dev simulations, not 2026:
  - the family level was moved from the declared raw 0.10 to a calibrated 0.05, because the raw 0.10 gate falsely adopts 21% of the time;
  - Holm at family-wise 0.10 across issues;
  - block lengths 10 and 20.
  These changes are listed in PROTOCOL.md as deviations from candidates.md.
- **Holm depends on bookkeeping.** It only works if every fan-out agent logs every declared family in the ledger. Unlogged informal ideas form a hidden family.
- **Assumptions of the H1 power analysis.** It assumes rho is about 0.55 and stays stable. The resampling DGPs came out at rho of about 0.53. If prospective rho is nearer 0.50, 300 sessions is underpowered, and 400 is safer. The percentile CI undercovers slightly (0.89-0.94 at 300-400 sessions), which makes the pass mildly liberal.
- **H2 criterion.** The point-in-band H2 criterion passes 50% of the time when the true slope is 0.8, so a P-H2 pass is weak evidence.
- **Estimation window.** Re-estimating v3 on data through 2026-11-23 is estimation, not selection, but it changes M's yardstick relative to v2. The prospective comparison with v2-frozen must be on Spearman of changes or levels, not on thresholds.
- **Monte Carlo precision.** MC s.e. is 0.7-1.6% on size and 2-3% on power. Parametric DGPs assume AR(1), t5 and equicorrelation.
- **S0 vs S1.** The calibrated p of 0.047 is borderline; "look-ahead, not a better model" rests on mechanism (per-fold and episode decomposition) plus a post-hoc 2026 diagnostic, not on a clean test.

verdicts.issue: MARKET AGGREGATION (H1b): v2 M lost to v1 on 2026 five-session changes
verdicts.proposal: Labelled 'no change', which keeps logit breadth BL as the aggregate. The operative recommendation is to ship M_v3 = (BL - mu_dev)/sd_dev on a fixed linear yardstick instead of v2's percentile-mapped M = Phi^-1(F_dev(BL)). F_M stays as a display percentile. C1-C4 are not adopted.
verdicts.reasons:
REPRODUCED independently from the committed outputs/dev/walkforward_daily.npz plus each fold's m_map in the shared cache (critic/mkt_check.py, mkt_check.json). On 363 within-block 5-session changes, M_foldmap minus BL Spearman = -0.0428 (paired stationary bootstrap, block 20, 2000 resamples: s.e. 0.0149, z -2.86, 95% CI -0.071 to -0.012). All three folds are negative: -0.013 (z -1.3), -0.016 (z -0.7), -0.074 (z -4.0). Leaving out any one month keeps it between -0.050 and -0.034. BL minus Mleg = +0.0374 (s.e. 0.0165), which matches the committed +0.037. M_foldmap minus Mleg = -0.005 (s.e. 0.016). So the object v2 shipped was never the one that won on dev, and that mismatch is real.

FAMILY GATE (critic/mkt_gate.py): with the shipped M as incumbent, I ran spa_functional_calibrated (block 20, B=R=299) on the family {BL, C1..C4}. Gains are +0.043 (t 2.99), +0.044 (3.01), -0.004, +0.013 and -0.017. Raw and calibrated p are both below 1/299 (0.0034). BL alone gives the same. It clears Holm.

REFUTATION POINTS:
(1) Calling this 'no change' is a framing choice. Relative to what was published and pre-registered (M), it is a change and must go in the ledger as one. The agent moved the baseline from the shipped M to the dev-selected BL, and that move is what turns the fix into 'no change'.
(2) The discovery came from 2026, and this is admitted. The evidence is dev out-of-sample and was declared before scoring (candidates.md 22:47:57 precedes diagnosis.json 22:49:44 and score_results.json 22:51:44). The object is the one dev selected before 2026, so this is not a new fit to 2026.
(3) Fold C (2025H2) carries most of the effect. Folds A and B are individually not significant.
(4) Including the reference comparison, K=5 objects were compared, one more than the 4-candidate cap.
(5) The gain-profile mechanism (a concave map against VXN's convex response) is post hoc and was measured on the validation target. It is plausible but unconfirmed.
(6) Raw-B C1 ties BL on dev (+0.0009 standardised per fold; +0.006, s.e. 0.005 raw) and won post hoc in 2026, so choosing C1 would be 2026-driven. Ship BL, the object dev selected, not C1.
verdicts.required_checks: Ledger it as v3 change #1 with incumbent = published M, and name it a fix of the mismatch between the selected and the shipped object, not 'no change'. Define bands and alerts in BL or F_M units (M>=2 corresponds to BL>=1.2376, i.e. F_M>=97.7), never as 'M_v3>=2'. Under the P1 rule, re-estimate mu and sd on 2023-01..2026-11. Pre-register H1' on M_v3 with v2-frozen M and v1 as prospective comparators. Report the 2026 values (0.603, and H1b +0.020 with CI -0.024 to +0.062) only as post-hoc. Make no H1b 'better' claim. REPRODUCED EXACTLY with a separate implementation (critic/vol_check.py, vol_check.json): the B0, C1, C2 and C3 forecasts match the agent's to a max abs difference of 0.0.
